target_customer: Consumer subscription media businesses such as publishers and streaming services (The Atlantic, Daily Mail, Hearst, NBCUniversal)
problem: Subscription media teams struggle to run retention experiments and personalized journeys without engineering help. Subsets predicts churn risk and automates lifecycle experiments.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for retention and lifecycle automation
product_category: AI retention and lifecycle growth platform

founders.name: Martin Johnsen
education: Technical University of Denmark, MSc Mathematical Modeling
founders.background_notes: YC page says he worked in management consulting helping large organizations scale AI. Employer not named.

founders.name: Oliver Brandt
founders.background_notes: YC page says machine learning engineer background, employer not named.

founders.name: Nikolai Skelbo
founders.background_notes: YC page says growth and revenue operations experience at a SaaS scale-up, not named.

founders.name: Matias
education: Computer science degree, school not named
founders.background_notes: Named only as Matias in the YC launch post; Seedtable gives the surname Ebbesen. Not in the YC active founders list.

technical_complexity.rationale: Churn prediction with explainable machine learning plus integrations to subscription, product and CRM data; standard ML engineering with some hard integration work.

defensibility.rationale: Integration into customers' data stack and accumulated experiment data raise switching costs; marketing automation vendors could add similar features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Aggregator lists name Iterable and Retention Genius as alternatives; no acquisition or copying found.

market_need_then: Subscription media competes on churn and lifetime value; named customers publish retention goals. No dated 2023 source on the market was found.

branding.name_origin: TechCrunch says the product lets teams run retention experiments on subsets of a subscriber base, hence the name.
branding.domain_note: Uses subsets.com, an exact match dot com.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and benefit focused, mixing British and American spelling

brand_strength.rationale: The name fits the product and the exact dot com is owned, but the word is generic and no brand press was found.

outcome_analysis: Subsets moved from San Francisco to Copenhagen after YC S23, raised a confirmed $1.65M pre-seed in February 2024 and lists premium publishers as customers, with a seven person team. The YC page claims $6.1M raised but only the pre-seed is sourced, so later rounds are unknown. It remains active with no exit.
notes: The YC page and its description say $6.1M raised, The Hub says EUR 6.1M, LinkedIn $6.4M, CB Insights $2.15M over two rounds, Seedtable $3.9M over three rounds; none beyond the $1.65M pre-seed is sourced to a primary release. The company blog and TechCrunch both confirm the pre-seed. Competitor lists come from low quality aggregators without 2023 dates, so the list is empty. Founding year conflicts (2022 or 2023).
